You receive 2 images. Image 1 is a finished background painting of our point-and-click adventure game: Dúbravská zastávka in 1995. Image 2 is the same painting with coloured boxes that only mark where the interactive objects of the new version must be. Edit image 1 into the SAME PLACE in 1982, seen by the SAME CAMERA: keep the exact viewpoint, lens, horizon, perspective and framing, and keep the position, size and outline of every building, wall, kerb, step, door, window, pole, rail and tree trunk that exists in both eras. Change only what the time changes, as described below. Keep the painting technique, brushwork, palette handling and level of detail of image 1.

The fixed landmark 'curb' stays exactly at x 236, y 802 (12 % from the left, 74 % from the top). The fixed landmark 'track_line' stays exactly at x 1540, y 774 (80 % from the left, 72 % from the top). The fixed landmark 'clock_frame' stays exactly at x 679, y 147 (35 % from the left, 14 % from the top).

Era changes: the same place on an early-December afternoon in 1982, cold and calm: pale low winter sun through a thin haze, soft long shadows, bare grey-brown lindens, maples and birches, a thin layer of old snow lying on the lawns, along the kerbs, on the roofs and in the corners of the platform, the platform itself mostly clear and damp. The tram line to Dubravka does NOT exist yet - it is being built:
- The track bed at the right is a building site: fresh gravel and sand, a few of the big grey concrete track panels already laid on the near side, more concrete panels and rails stacked beside the far track, no rails on the far track yet, no overhead wires; the tall lamp posts stand, but no wires hang between them. A low red-and-white striped wooden construction barrier runs along the platform's right edge, with one small white board on it with the black words STAVBA ELEKTRIČKOVEJ TRATE.
- No tram: where the 1995 tram stood, paint the building site, the bare trees, the east carriageway and the medical centre behind it.
- The platform slabs are new concrete; the low concrete kerb block at the near left with its chipped corner, the ramp and the zebra crossing are the same.
- An older, simpler shelter stands in exactly the same place and footprint: a plain dark green steel frame with a flat roof and clear glass panels, a simple wooden bench inside; through its glass the road behind shows.
- On the west carriageway at the left, beside the platform, an articulated city bus of the period (Ikarus 280 type: boxy, cream-white upper body and dark red lower body, big flat windscreen, no logos, no number, blank destination box) waits at a temporary bus stop, its front towards the camera, its front part fully visible between the left frame edge and the shelter's near end, the rest hidden behind the shelter; a small round temporary bus-stop sign on a post beside it (bus pictogram only).
- The stop post in the same place carries the same round brass clock on top, a small white plate with a bus pictogram, and a small glazed case with a paper timetable.
- Beyond the building site, on the green strip in front of the medical centre, a large red slogan billboard on two legs faces the stop, with neat white capital letters: ZA SPOLOČNÚ BUDÚCNOSŤ.
- The low bluish two-storey medical centre on the right (its long white ribbon windows and blue-grey mosaic tiles) and the long panel block with the red-orange balconies behind it already stand, new and clean, in exactly the same places.
- One or two period cars (small boxy 1970s sedans, beige and pale blue) on the east carriageway at the right. No people.
Everything else built (the platform, the kerb block, the ramp and zebra crossing, the roads rising up the hill, the towers, the medical centre, the lamp posts) stays exactly where it is.

Interactive props of 1982:
1. the box labelled 'Dobové heslo' in image 2 (x 1160-1356, y 318-436 of the 1920x1080 frame (60-71 % from the left, 29-40 % from the top)): the red slogan billboard with the white words ZA SPOLOČNÚ BUDÚCNOSŤ, the whole billboard inside the box.
2. the box labelled 'Papierový poriadok' in image 2 (x 614-742, y 440-580 of the 1920x1080 frame (32-39 % from the left, 41-54 % from the top)): the small glazed case on the stop post with a typed paper timetable (illegible lines, no digits).
the box labelled 'exit: Pred ZŠ Sokolíkova v roku 1982' in image 2 (x 0-250, y 760-960 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-13 % from the left, 70-89 % from the top)) is the ramp and zebra crossing at the near left (towards the school). the box labelled 'exit: Sídliskový obchod v roku 1982' in image 2 (x 780-1020, y 430-642 of the 1920x1080 frame (41-53 % from the left, 40-59 % from the top)) is the far end of the platform.

Walkable floor: the band at x 0-1262, y 664-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-66 % from the left, 61-94 % from the top) stays the open, flat platform with nothing standing on it, only light, shadows and a few small patches of old snow at its edges.
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: no stop name, no transport-company logos, no line numbers, no brands, no shop signs, no lettering on the medical centre, no number plates, no people, no animals. Apart from the two inscriptions asked for above, any paper shows only illegible scribbles, no digits.

Image 2 is a positioning aid only: do NOT draw any of its boxes, outlines, labels or captions. The result is image 1 edited, in the same 16:9 framing: no frames, no borders, no UI, no captions, no watermark, no text except what is asked for above, and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
